root_cause.confirmed: Two packages named `careervp` exist and are disjoint except for __init__: src/backend/careervp (has `handlers`, no `naming_utils`/`service_stack`) and infra/careervp (the reverse). Only one can own sys.modules['careervp'].
root_cause.the_bug: CDK-synth tests put infra/ at sys.path[0] and evicted every cached careervp* module resolved from elsewhere, then never restored. sys.modules['careervp'] stayed bound to infra's package for the rest of the process, so every later `import careervp.handlers.*` raised ModuleNotFoundError.
root_cause.why_isolated_runs_passed: tests/conftest.py:13 imports the backend's careervp at module level, so a process starts with the backend's cached. The bug only bites once something evicts that cache later.

finding_1_ten_files_not_eight.method: grep -rln 'sys\.modules\.pop\|del sys\.modules' tests/ — a whole-tree sweep rather than checking only the named list

group_b_victim.note: Inserted INFRA_SRC without evicting, and is the only test needing BOTH packages in sequence: infra's to synthesize the stack, then the backend's to import the Handler string the stack points at. That is why it was the canary.

group_c_the_missed_one.why_it_matters: NOT in handoff 01's list. It runs the exact mirror image — prefers BACKEND_SRC and evicts everything resolved from elsewhere — also without restoring. It lives in tests/unit, the 1430-test directory.
group_c_the_missed_one.significance: This is the second, independent contamination source handoff 01's Finding 2 predicted. It is not a different mechanism; it is the same mechanism pointing the opposite way. Two unrestored evictors fighting is precisely why whole-suite counts moved by ~200 between runs once pytest-randomly was enabled: the result depended on which of the two ran last.

finding_2_the_eviction_was_probably_neve.observation: With only the backend's careervp cached, `from careervp.naming_utils import NamingUtils` still resolves — to infra's file.
finding_2_the_eviction_was_probably_neve.mechanism: The backend venv has an editable-install meta_path finder, __editable___service_cdk_1_0_finder._EditableFinder, whose MAPPING sends the bare name 'careervp' to /infra/careervp. PathFinder is consulted first and searches the cached package's __path__ (backend); on a miss the editable finder answers, so infra submodules resolve without any eviction at all.
finding_2_the_eviction_was_probably_neve.collision_check: Submodule names are disjoint. backend: dal, handlers, infrastructure, logic, models, payment_providers, validation. infra: ai_assist_nested_stack, api_construct, api_db_construct, artifact_chain_construct, cognito_construct, company_research_nested_stack, configuration, constants, crud_features_nested_stack, error_report_nested_stack, frontend_stack, monitoring, naming_utils, rehome_map, scratch_deployment, service_stack, specs, utils, waf_construct. Only __init__ collides.
finding_2_the_eviction_was_probably_neve.implication: The eviction dance's only real effect was to rebind sys.modules['careervp'] itself — which nothing needed. Deleting it outright was very likely safe.
finding_2_the_eviction_was_probably_neve.decision_and_why: NOT taken. The minimal behavior-preserving fix (wrap the existing switch in a restoring context manager) was shipped instead. Removing the dance entirely is a larger behavioral bet that would need its own proof, and the handoff's ground rules say to stop and report rather than redesign unilaterally. Recorded here as a cheap follow-up for whoever wants it.

helper.behavior: Snapshots sys.path and every careervp* sys.modules entry on entry; performs the same switch as before; in a finally, deletes whatever careervp* modules exist and restores the snapshot verbatim, then restores sys.path wholesale.

what_success_looked_like_vs_what_happene.why_the_expectation_was_conservative: The handoff modelled the 601 failures as a mix of contamination and genuine order-independent product-code assertions, and expected only the ~100 errors to be contamination-shaped. In fact all 701 red items shared the single root cause: a test module that fails to import reports as an ERROR, but a test whose module imported fine and then hit a poisoned sys.modules mid-run reports as a FAILURE. what_success_looked_like_vs_what_happene.caveat: This also means the combined run had never been proving anything about product correctness. It is green now because the instrument was repaired, not because product code changed. No product code was touched in this handoff.
